edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); first published in New Youth (新青年), vol. 6, 1919, and collected in Call to Arms (吶喊), 1923.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；初刊于 1919 年《新青年》第六卷，收入《呐喊》（1923）。

basis.en: First published in 1919; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1919 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A failed scholar who drinks his wine standing in a long gown, the only customer who does, and who is laughed at until one day he simply stops coming. Lu Xun tells it through a bored twelve-year-old serving boy, which is what makes it so hard to read: the boy laughs too. Notice the board where his debt is chalked; nineteen coppers are the last trace he leaves.
note.zh: 一个没有进学的读书人，是酒店里唯一站着喝酒而穿长衫的人，被众人取笑，直到有一天不再来。鲁迅借一个无聊的十二岁小伙计来讲，这正是它难读的地方：孩子也跟着笑。留意那块记账的粉板，十九个钱是他留下的最后痕迹。

excerpt.orig: 孔乙己是這樣的使人快活，可是沒有他，別人也便這麽過。
excerpt.en: That was how Kong Yiji made people happy, but without him, they got along just as well.
excerpt.zh: 孔乙己是这样的使人快活，可是没有他，别人也便这么过。

gloss.en: Luzhen (Lu Town): the market town of several of Lu Xun's stories, drawn from the country around Shaoxing. Lu was his mother's surname, and he took it for his pen name too.
gloss.zh: 鲁镇：鲁迅好几篇小说里的市镇，取材于绍兴一带。“鲁”是他母亲的姓，他的笔名也取了这个字。

gloss.en: Aniseed beans: dried broad beans simmered with star anise or fennel and salt, still the snack sold with Shaoxing wine.
gloss.zh: 茴香豆：用茴香、盐等煮成的蚕豆，至今仍是绍兴人下酒的小吃。

gloss.en: The short-jacket crowd: labourers, who wore short jackets for work. A long gown marked a man of learning or leisure, which is why Kong Yiji keeps his, however ragged.
gloss.zh: 短衣帮：做工的人，干活穿短衣。长衫是读书人或有闲者的标志，所以孔乙己的长衫再破也不肯脱。

gloss.en: Xianheng, 'all things prosper', is a phrase from the Book of Changes. A tavern of this name stood near Lu Xun's family house in Shaoxing in the 1890s.
gloss.zh: 咸亨：语出《周易·坤卦》“品物咸亨”，意为万物皆得亨通。十九世纪九十年代，绍兴鲁迅家附近确有一家咸亨酒店。

gloss.en: Yellow wine: wine brewed from glutinous rice, the best known from Shaoxing, and drunk warm.
gloss.zh: 黄酒：用糯米等酿成的酒，以绍兴所产最有名，多温热了喝。

gloss.en: The opening of a traditional copybook that children traced over in red: 上大人，孔乙己，化三千，七十士… The characters were chosen for their few strokes; the lines are usually read as praise of Confucius and his three thousand pupils, and meant little to a child.
gloss.zh: 描红纸是儿童习字时照着描写的红字纸，开头是“上大人，孔乙己，化三千，七十士……”。这些字笔画简单，一般解作称颂孔子教化三千弟子，孩子们读来半懂不懂。

gloss.en: From the Analects (15.2): 'A gentleman holds firm in hardship; a small man in hardship loses all restraint.'
gloss.zh: 语出《论语·卫灵公》：“君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣。”

gloss.en: 進學: to pass the county examination and enter the official school as a licentiate (秀才), the first rung of the examination ladder.
gloss.zh: 进学：童生考中秀才，进入府、州、县学，是科举的第一步。

gloss.en: The four forms usually given are 回, 囘, 囬 and 𡇈.
gloss.zh: 通常举出的四种写法是：回、囘、囬、𡇈。

gloss.en: Kong Yiji is quoting the Analects (9.6), where Confucius says a gentleman does not need many skills: 'Many? Not many.' He turns it to the beans.
gloss.zh: 语出《论语·子罕》：“君子多乎哉？不多也。”孔子说君子不必多能，孔乙己借来说豆子。

gloss.en: 舉人: a provincial graduate, who had passed the second tier of the civil examinations and could be appointed to office; in a small town, a man of power.
gloss.zh: 举人：乡试考中的人，有做官的资格，在小镇上是有权势的人物。

gloss.en: Debts were settled three times a year in the old calendar: before the Dragon Boat Festival, before Mid-Autumn, and at the year's end, the 'year's pass'. The tavern keeper takes down his board at each.
gloss.zh: 旧时一年分三节结账：端午、中秋和年底，年底这一关叫“年关”。掌柜每到这时便取下粉板。
